items.definition:
a vehicle used for travel in outer space
Astronauts travel in a spaceship.

a tall North American plant of the daisy family, with very large golden-rayed flowers
The sunflower turned its head towards the sun.

a document connected to the World Wide Web and viewable with a web browser
You can find more information on our webpage.

a small, sweet, quick bread
I had a blueberry muffin for breakfast.

a large, round fruit with sweet, juicy red pulp and a green rind
We had watermelon for dessert.

An appliance or device for cooking food.
She bought a new slow cooker for her kitchen.

a tailless amphibian, similar to a frog
A toad hopped across the garden path.

a machine for washing clothes or dishes
The washer broke down.

The way someone acts.
His behaviour at the party was unacceptable.

the way in which someone's hair is cut or arranged
She changed her hairstyle for the party.

a powerful light at the front of a motor vehicle
The car's headlight was broken after the accident.

a small, oval fruit with a brown, hairy skin and green flesh; a flightless bird native to New Zealand
I like to eat kiwi fruit for breakfast.

a storm with thunder and lightning
We took shelter when the thunderstorm began.

a speech sound produced with an open vocal tract
The English alphabet has five main vowels: a, e, i, o, u.

a large reptile similar to a crocodile
We saw an alligator in the swamp.

a cover for holding loose papers
Please put all the documents in the binder.

a vegetable with long, crisp stalks
She added chopped celery to the soup.

a large African mammal with a very long neck and legs
We saw a tall giraffe at the zoo.

a large, round fruit with sweet, juicy flesh
I bought a sweet cantaloupe melon at the market.

a large deer with long antlers, found in arctic regions
Santa's sleigh is pulled by magical reindeer.

a person who skates, especially on ice or roller skates
The ice skater performed a beautiful routine.

a small, short-tailed rodent often kept as a pet
My sister got a new hamster for her birthday.

a private box for mail, or a public box for posting letters
I checked the mailbox for letters.

loose-fitting garments worn for sleeping
He changed into his pajamas before going to bed.

a male chicken
The rooster crowed loudly at dawn.

aunt (informal)
My auntie always bakes the best cookies.

a bird's mouth
The parrot used its strong beak to crack the nut.

a small, sweet, dark blue berry
I love to eat blueberries with my yogurt.

care provided during the day for children or elderly people
We send our daughter to daycare while we work.

a container with a handle and a lip, for holding and pouring liquids
Please fill the jug with water.

A coffee drink made with espresso and steamed milk.
I ordered a hot latte this morning.

A small pig (often used by children).
The little piggy went to market.

a small spoon used for stirring tea or coffee
Add one teaspoon of sugar to your coffee.

vegetable (informal)
Make sure you eat your greens and other veg.

a flat, crisp cake made from batter cooked in a waffle iron
I had a delicious waffle with syrup for breakfast.

a device consisting of two flexible strips of metal or plastic with interlocking projections, used for fastening or closing openings
My jacket zipper is broken.

a scale of temperature on which water freezes at 0° and boils at 100° under standard conditions
The temperature today is 25 degrees Celsius.

a firm, sharp-tasting cheese, originally made in Cheddar, Somerset, England
Would you like some cheddar cheese with your crackers.

a small, hot-tasting pod of a variety of capsicum, used in cooking
This dish is very spicy because it has a lot of chilli.

a machine for washing dishes
Please load the dishwasher after dinner.

a cream or lotion rubbed on the skin to protect it from the sun
Don't forget to apply sunscreen before going to the beach.

a racket sport
They played a game of badminton in the park.

a small, typically orange or gold, freshwater fish, often kept as a pet
My sister has a goldfish in a bowl.

salt, pepper, herbs, or spices added to food
Add some seasoning to the soup for more flavor.

a garment worn for swimming
Don't forget your swimsuit if you want to go to the beach.

a punctuation mark
Remember to use a comma before a coordinating conjunction.

the time between evening and morning
It's much colder during the nighttime.

a Mexican dish consisting of a tortilla wrapped around a filling
I had a delicious chicken burrito for lunch.

a person who camps, or a vehicle designed for camping
We saw a group of campers setting up their tents by the lake.

person who installs/repairs electrical wiring
We called an electrician to fix the faulty wiring.

a small pool of liquid, especially rain
The children jumped in the puddles after the rain.

a person who greets and assists visitors
The receptionist greeted us with a smile.

a slow-moving reptile
The tortoise slowly made its way across the garden.

kilogram (unit of mass)
I need two kilos of apples.

A thick, smooth drink made of fresh fruit pureed with milk, yogurt, or ice cream.
I like to drink a fruit smoothie for breakfast.

a single crystal of snow
Each snowflake has a unique pattern.

the period of summer
We love going to the beach in the summertime.

a strip of material used to bind up a wound or to protect an injured part of the body
He wrapped a bandage around his sprained ankle.

a unit of length, equal to one hundredth of a meter
The ruler was marked in centimeters.

a shaped piece of wood, plastic, or wire with a hook at the top, used for hanging clothes
Please put your coat on a hanger.

a unit of mass equal to 1,000 grams
The package weighed five kilograms.

a thick, creamy dressing consisting of egg yolks, oil, vinegar, and seasonings
Would you like some mayonnaise with your fries?

a strip of hair left to grow above the upper lip
He decided to grow a moustache for Movember.

A four-sided shape
A book usually has the shape of a rectangle.
